The KOKKOS buffer row has fixed stride 'elements = size_border + size_velocity', so the shortfall does not spill into the next atom, but every field packed after v inside the same row (angmom, molecule, q, mu, sp, radius, rmass, omega, DPD) is written 3 slots too early, while AtomVecKokkos_UnpackBorderVel unconditionally reads 3 velocity slots and then the remaining fields at the nominal offsets. Verify the AtomVec is destroyed before Kokkos::finalize() (LAMMPS deletes atom before tearing down KokkosLMP), otherwise the free must move into a pre-finalize hook.

src/fix_nve_sphere.cpp has two enums, 'enum{NONE,DIPOLE};' and 'enum{NODLM,DLM};', and its constructor (lines 53-57) maps 'update dipole' to extra=DIPOLE and 'update dipole/dlm' to extra=DIPOLE AND dlm=DLM. FixNVESphere::initial_integrate then branches 'if (dlm == NODLM) {...cross-product + renormalize...} else {...Dullweber-Leimkuhler-Maclachlan rotation, which also writes back omega[i][0..2] from the rotated body-frame angular velocity...}'. src/KOKKOS/fix_nve_sphere_kokkos.cpp declares only 'enum{NONE,DIPOLE};' (line 23) and grep for 'dlm' in the KOKKOS file returns nothing; initial_integrate_item (line ~115) has a single 'if (extra == DIPOLE)' block containing the NODLM cross-product update. FixNVESphereKokkos::init() just forwards to FixNVESphere::init(), and neither constructor nor init rejects dlm==DLM, so 'fix nve/sphere/kk ... update dipole/dlm' runs the wrong (non-symplectic) integrator with no warning, and omega gets only the torque increment. Adjustment: the finding is right but understates the damage — the KOKKOS DIPOLE block also drops the CPU's 'if (mu[i][3] > 0.0)' guard, so a sphere with a zero dipole gives msq==0 and scale = mu(i,3)/sqrt(0) = 0/0 = NaN, poisoning mu for that atom. That affects plain 'update dipole' too, not just dlm.
fix: Two edits. (1) Either implement the DLM branch in FixNVESphereKokkos::initial_integrate_item (port the Q/R rotation sequence from src/fix_nve_sphere.cpp:160-266, updating both omega and mu), or, as an interim measure, make FixNVESphereKokkos::init() call error->all(FLERR, "Fix nve/sphere/kk does not support the dipole/dlm option") when dlm == DLM. (2) Independently, guard the existing dipole block with 'if (mu(i,3) > 0.0)' to match the CPU style.

The base class src/fix_nve_sphere.cpp sets dlm=DLM for the 'dipole/dlm' keyword (line 54-57) and selects a completely different Dullweber-Leimkuhler-Maclachlan rotation in initial_integrate (line 160 onward), which also rewrites omega. Nothing in the KOKKOS constructor or init() rejects the combination, so the option is silently ignored.

reasoning: ComputeTempDeformKokkos<DeviceType>::remove_deform_bias_all_kk (lines 173-198) syncs and binds the DeviceType views ('atomKK->sync(execution_space,X_MASK|V_MASK|MASK_MASK); x = atomKK->k_x.view<DeviceType>();'), then calls 'domainKK->x2lamda(nlocal);' before launching Kokkos::parallel_for on RangePolicy<DeviceType,...>. So it converts only the device copy and marks the DEVICE copy modified, leaving the host mirror holding Cartesian coordinates. The file instantiates ComputeTempDeformKokkos<LMPHostType> under '#ifdef LMP_KOKKOS_GPU', and in that build LMPHostType != LMPDeviceType so the two x mirrors are distinct memory. The TagComputeTempDeformRemoveBias kernel then reads the stale Cartesian host x and computes vbiasall from Cartesian rather than lamda coordinates. On a CPU-only Kokkos build the mirrors alias and the bug is invisible, which is why it survives testing.

Cache domain->h_inv and domain->boxlo in KK_FLOAT members before the launch and inline 'lamda = h_inv * (x - boxlo)' (the TagDomain_x2lamda body) in TagComputeTempDeformRemoveBias, then delete the domainKK->x2lamda(nlocal)/lamda2x(nlocal) pair. That fixes F0091 at the same time. If the round trip is kept instead, x2lamda/lamda2x must be made DeviceType-aware (or the compute must sync/modify X in the correct space around them).

reasoning: ComputeTempDeformKokkos::remove_deform_bias_all_kk brackets its kernel with 'domainKK->x2lamda(nlocal);' (line 186) and 'domainKK->lamda2x(nlocal);' (line 195), i.e. it rewrites every local atom's coordinates in place and converts them back. The CPU style never touches atom->x: ComputeTempDeform::remove_bias_all (src/compute_temp_deform.cpp:307-317) declares 'double lamda[3];' and calls 'domain->x2lamda(atom->x[i], lamda);' into that local, as do compute_scalar/compute_vector/remove_bias/restore_bias (lines 256, 275, 313, 354). The KOKKOS round trip therefore perturbs atom->x by the round-off of two matrix transforms — amplified here because k_x holds KK_FLOAT, which is single precision in a mixed/float build — and additionally costs two extra full-array device passes plus X_MASK sync traffic per call. Confirmed as described; impact is small in a double build, hence low.
fix: Same edit as F0078: compute the lamda coordinate inside TagComputeTempDeformRemoveBias from cached h_inv/boxlo instead of converting atom->x in place, and remove the x2lamda/lamda2x pair. This makes the KOKKOS style bit-comparable to the CPU one and removes the host/device divergence of F0078.
